children: Thailand’s S&P Global Manufacturing PMI rose to 54.8 in October 2026 from 54.3 in the previous month, marking its highest level since December 2025, as demand conditions continued to improve.
New orders increased at one of the fastest rates on record, supported by an expanding customer base and successful promotional efforts.
In response to stronger production requirements and inventory replenishment needs, manufacturers ramped up purchasing activity at the fastest pace since August 2024.
However, outstanding business accumulated at its fastest rate in nearly a year, as rising workloads were compounded by reduced workforce capacity amid staff resignations.
On the price front, input costs edged up, reflecting higher raw material prices.
Meanwhile, manufacturers largely kept selling prices unchanged to support sales.
Lastly, business confidence remained positive in October, with firms maintaining strong expectations for output growth over the next 12 months.

title: Thailand Manufacturing Sector at 10-Month High
